Task: Add self-hosted Loopy causal-loop-diagram embeds to the Astro site.

Loopy (https://github.com/ncase/loopy) is a self-contained vanilla-JS tool for interactive causal loop diagrams. I want to embed animated CLDs in blog posts without depending on ncase.me at runtime. Loopy has no external dependencies; every script/CSS it loads is a relative local path, so self-hosting gives identical play/animation functionality.

Step 1: Vendor the Loopy app into public/.

git clone --depth 1 --branch gh-pages https://github.com/ncase/loopy.git /tmp/loopy
mkdir -p public/loopy
cp -r /tmp/loopy/v1.1 public/loopy/v1.1
Copy the whole v1.1/ folder (all of js/ and css/), not just index.html, or it breaks. Check /tmp/loopy/LICENSE.txt and preserve attribution as it requires.

Step 2: Add a reusable component src/components/Loopy.astro:

---
const { data, height = 520, title = "Causal loop diagram" } = Astro.props;
---
<iframe
  src={`/loopy/v1.1/?embed=1&data=${data}`}
  title={title}
  width="100%" height={height}
  style="border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:8px" loading="lazy">
</iframe>
The embed=1 param is Loopy's embed mode: it hides the editing chrome but keeps the simulation (play/pause + drag-a-node-to-perturb).

Step 3: Verify. Run the dev server, add the component to a scratch/test MDX page with the data value below, and confirm: nodes render with colours, the diagram animates, and dragging "Bed Occupancy" up amplifies the reinforcing loop. Then remove the scratch page.

Test model (Ontario ER "Bed Occupancy + R1 Staffing Spiral" CLD), pass as the data prop (note the double-encoded %2520 form is correct for the URL):

[[[1,500,320,1,%22Bed%2520Occupancy%22,0],[2,230,130,1,%22Hospital%2520Admissions%22,5],[3,500,110,1,%22LTC%2520Waitlist%22,3],[4,780,130,1,%22Bed%2520Supply%2520per%2520Capita%22,4],[5,790,360,1,%22Staff%2520Burnout%22,0],[6,770,575,1,%22Staffing%2520Levels%22,5],[7,500,600,1,%22Staffed%2520Beds%22,5],[8,240,470,1,%22ER%2520Crowding%22,0]],[[2,1,0,1],[3,1,0,1],[4,1,0,-1],[1,5,50,1],[5,6,50,-1],[6,7,50,1],[7,1,50,-1],[1,8,0,1]],[[640,470,%22R1%253A%2520Staffing%2520Spiral%250A(reinforcing)%22]],9%5D]
Usage in MDX:

import Loopy from "../../components/Loopy.astro";

<Loopy data="[[[1,500,320,1,%22Bed%2520Occupancy%22,0]...9%5D]" height={520} />
Loopy data format reference (in case you edit models by hand): the model is [nodes, edges, labels, UID]. Node = [id, x, y, initValue, doubleEncodedLabel, hue] where hue is 0=red 1=orange 2=yellow 3=green 4=blue 5=purple. Edge = [from, to, arc, strength] where strength +1 = same-direction link, -1 = opposite. Label = [x, y, doubleEncodedText]. In the URL the whole thing is JSON with quotes written as %22 and the trailing ] as %5D, and label text double-URL-encoded.

CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Yes, it fits, and it's genuinely responsive. Here's the mechanism and the one caveat.

## Why it fits

- **Width:** the iframe is `width:100%`, and the wrapper is a normal block element, so it fills whatever content column it's dropped into. In a blog post the prose container is `max-w-none` (it takes the article column width, not a 65ch cap), so the embed spans the full text width. Same for normal pages.
- **Content scaling:** this is the important part. In embed mode Loopy calls `model.center(true)` on load **and re-subscribes it to every `resize`** (`Loopy.js:225-230`). The `true` triggers scale-to-fit in `Model.center` (`Model.js:519-540`): it measures the diagram's bounding box, compares aspect ratios, and scales by the *smaller* of the width-fit / height-fit ratio. So the whole diagram always shrinks to fit the iframe's box (minus padding), aspect preserved, **nothing clipped** — at any column width down to mobile. Because it's wired to `resize`, it re-fits live when the viewport changes.

So: full-width desktop column → diagram fills it; narrow mobile column → same diagram, scaled down to fit. No horizontal overflow either way.

## The one caveat: legibility, not fit

Because it scales the *entire* fixed-coordinate diagram to fit, on a narrow column (phones, ~350px) an 8-node model like this gets small — node labels become hard to read. Fit is never the problem; readability at small widths is. Two practical levers:

- **Height** is fixed by the `height` prop (default 520). On a fit-by-width diagram (this model is slightly wider than tall), extra height just adds vertical whitespace, so 520 is about right here; bump it only for tall/dense models.
- **Node count** is the real driver. This ~8-node model reads fine in a desktop article column. If you build a 15+ node diagram, consider giving it more height, or accept that mobile readers will pinch-zoom.

No component change needed — it works in a blog post or page as-is. If you want, I can add a small responsive tweak (e.g. a taller `height` on mobile via a `min-height`/aspect wrapper) but I'd only do that once you have a model that actually needs it, rather than guessing now.

content.text: Where do I add a loopy? as a file or as text in the blog post/page?

Inline text, not a file. The model lives right in the `.mdx` file as a string prop — there's no separate `.loopy` file to manage.

## How to add one

Both blog posts (`src/content/blog/{slug}/index.mdx`) and pages (`src/content/pages/{slug}/index.mdx`) are MDX, so you can import components. Two steps:

**1. Import once, at the top of the file (below the frontmatter):**

```mdx
import Loopy from '@/components/global/Loopy.astro';
```

(Straight quotes in the import, per the usual rule. `@/` resolves to `src/`.)

**2. Drop the component wherever you want the diagram in the body:**

```mdx
<Loopy
  data="[[[1,500,320,1,%22Bed%2520Occupancy%22,0], ...rest of model..., 9%5D]"
  title="Ontario ER staffing spiral"
/>
```
